text: Task 9 — Segmenting an Image Using K-Means A wildlife researcher receives a color photograph and wants to simplify it into a small number of visually meaningful regions. A single threshold is not appropriate because many different colors and intensity values occur in the image. The researcher decides to cluster pixels according to their color similarity . Use a complex color image such as: Your Task Implement K-Means-based image segmentation. Your 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. program should: Load a color image. Represent the image as a set of pixel feature vectors. Convert the pixel data to the appropriate numeric type. Perform K-Means clustering. Reconstruct the segmented image using cluster centers. Run the experiment for: K = 2, 4 and 6 Required Output Display : Original K=2 K=6 For each K, record: Number of clusters • Visual difference from the original • Amount of color simplification • Major regions represented by the clusters The procedure should follow the K-Means workflow in the manual : reshape pixels, convert to float32, cluster, obtain centers, and reconstruct the image .
